title: Phosphorus: ranges, compartments and absorption
sec: Phosphorus: ranges, compartments and absorption · p887
guide: Compare Ca and phosphate stores, albumin binding and intestinal fractions. Serum phosphate assays measure inorganic extracellular phosphate; do not apply the calcium correction formula to phosphate.

title: Renal phosphate and the FGF23–Klotho axis
sec: Renal phosphate and the FGF23–Klotho axis · p888
guide: Follow PCT transport through Fanconi syndrome, compensatory phosphaturia in early CKD and impaired signaling in advanced CKD. Distinguish medial vascular calcification from atherosclerotic intimal calcification.

title: Hyperphosphatemia: causes, calcinosis and binders
sec: Hyperphosphatemia: causes, calcinosis and binders · p889
guide: Trace increased intake, reduced excretion, cell release and calcitriol-driven absorption. Familial tumoral calcinosis is contrasted with phosphate-wasting FGF23 disorders. Prefer non-calcium binders when calcium loading is a concern.

title: Phosphate removal, depletion and redistribution
sec: Phosphate removal, depletion and redistribution · p890
guide: Diet and dialysis address phosphate excess. Severe depletion affects growth, RBCs, skeletal and cardiac muscle and insulin sensitivity. Understand the two directions linking phosphate and rhabdomyolysis.

title: Phosphate wasting, inherited rickets and replacement
sec: Phosphate wasting, inherited rickets and replacement · p891
guide: Read inheritance and gene pairs, then the common biochemical phenotype. The table contains a reversed FGF23 arrow: reduced cleavage must not be taught as low active FGF23. Tumor-induced osteomalacia reflects excess tumor-derived FGF23, not a mandatory germline mutation.
